A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Text, equations, seven tables, two figures, and all appendices are readable and matchable. v1 Appendices A–D correspond to v2 Appendices B–E; v2 adds a new Appendix A.

before.justification: v1 reports original DG and UDA experiments across six datasets, together with correlation analyses, controlled comparisons, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 2 and Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: The constrained kernel k-means procedure, linear-programming assignments, label and optional domain constraints, Nyström approximation, and soft-constraint option remain unchanged. The expanded mathematical justification does not introduce an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Both evaluate DG on Camelyon17, Humpbacks, and SVIRO, and UDA on VLCS, PACS, and Terra Incognita. The new discussion of ecological distribution shifts characterizes retained datasets rather than adding test scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain random splitting, leave-one-domain-out, mix-up, oracle selection, and the linear/RBF clustering variants. Newly cited algorithms do not appear as additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The CORAL/DANN setups, dataset sizes, preprocessing, architectures, and evaluation procedures are retained. Table 3 preserves the ten-configuration search, 3,000 training and finetuning steps, holdout fractions, kernel bandwidth, and Nyström subset size.

E4.justification: Both retain the MMD correlation analysis, oracle control for changing training distributions, worst-domain validation comparison, VLCS ablations, and Camelyon17 constraint analysis. The appendix analyses are relocated and relabeled without changed evidence.

E5.justification: Both report three trials, DomainBed standard errors, the same 95% confidence-interval comparison convention, and correlation coefficients with p-values. The uncertainty reporting practices and plotted statistics are unchanged.

E6.justification: All tabulated experimental values and both plot images are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains average accuracies of 77.7% for linear clustering and 77.0% for RBF clustering, and the combined Spearman correlation remains approximately 0.63.

T1.justification: v2 adds a formal DRO minimax formulation and a cited domain-adaptation error bound in Section 1.2. It replaces v1's brief MMD–clustering equivalence argument with the explicit identity in Equation (6) and a full Appendix A derivation, and expands the convergence argument into a finite-iteration proof sketch. These substantially extend the formal justification.

C1.justification: Despite the revised title and foregrounded theoretical motivation, the core contributions remain constrained clustering for model selection, convergence guarantees, DG/UDA performance advantages, and the MMD–accuracy association. Metadata independence and the clustering equivalence were already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds a qualification about maximizing MMD versus the error bound, a tentative explanation that domain-based uncertainty sets offer too few degrees of freedom for worst-domain validation to help, and discussion of conditional shifts in ecological datasets. The principal experimental interpretations and Section 2.5 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Training details, the Humpbacks processing/CNN pipeline, DomainBed and Gurobi identification, dataset licenses, and the 5,160-model/100-GPU-day computation disclosure are retained. Moving the implementation appendix from A to B does not change reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens the theoretical positioning through explicit DRO and domain-adaptation connections, citing Rahimian and Mehrotra, Ben-David et al., and Redko et al. It also acknowledges Bennett et al.'s constrained-clustering LP precedent and adds Gu et al. and Pfohl et al., while retaining the earlier validation-strategy literature.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are revised, preliminaries move before prior work, constraint definitions move into problem formulation, and dataset subheadings are simplified. Citation style changes to author–year. These are localized editorial and organizational changes; most existing prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, extensively reflowing equations and relocating tables and figures. Figure 1 is enlarged, Figure 2 becomes column-width, and appendix tables are redistributed. The underlying plots and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: Equation (6), Appendix A, and the expanded convergence discussion make the existing mathematical argument easier to inspect, while the added literature improves attribution and context. These provide a limited quality gain for an otherwise unchanged empirical contribution. The DRO/error-bound connection remains a heuristic motivation rather than a demonstrated guarantee of worst-case validation performance.
